problem.name_latex: Bounded distance decoding on periodic integer lattices
problem.name: Bounded distance decoding on periodic integer lattices
problem.statement_latex: Given an integer lattice $L\subseteq\mathbb Z^n$ with $q\mathbb Z^n\subseteq L$ and a target $t$ promised to satisfy $\operatorname{dist}(t,L)<\rho\lambda_1(L)$ for $\rho<1/2$, recover its unique closest lattice vector. Let $k$ be the minimum number of generators of the finite group $L/q\mathbb Z^n$. Complexity is measured in quantum gates and classical bit operations, polynomial in the lattice encoding and $\log q$.
problem.statement_text: Given an integer lattice $L\subseteq\mathbb Z^n$ with $q\mathbb Z^n\subseteq L$ and a target $t$ promised to satisfy $\operatorname{dist}(t,L)<\rho\lambda_1(L)$ for $\rho<1/2$, recover its unique closest lattice vector. Let $k$ be the minimum number of generators of the finite group $L/q\mathbb Z^n$. Complexity is measured in quantum gates and classical bit operations, polynomial in the lattice encoding and $\log q$.

quantum.details_latex: The decoding radius is $\lambda_1(L)2^{-\Omega(\sqrt{k\log q})}$, with the explicit constants and parameter restrictions of the theorem. The algorithm uses the finite-group structure of the $q$-periodic integer lattice and returns the closest vector under this promise. Basis encoding and the accuracy needed for quantum-state preparation enter the polynomial factors.

classical.headline_latex: Deterministic polynomial time in the same radius regime, Ducas--van Woerden decoding as developed by Allen et al.
classical.details_latex: The classical construction combines lattice reduction, duality, short full-rank vector sets and Babai nearest plane. The short-basis guarantee ensures correct rounding throughout the promised radius. Both bounds concern the same periodic-lattice parameters $n,k,q$ and exact recovery within the stated distance.

evidence.description_latex: Rigorous classical matching of the quantum decoding regime. The formal radius and input representation specify the scope of both polynomial-time statements.

hardware.description_latex: The quantum construction uses polynomial logical space, coherent algebraic arithmetic and Fourier processing. Its implementation would require controlled state preparation and fault-tolerant arithmetic at large dimension. The classical reduced-basis method implements the same decoding guarantee on ordinary hardware.
